description: Test your knowledge of Second week of development.

cards.text: When does implantation occur and what is the implantation window?
cards.answer: Implantation occurs Days 6–10 post-fertilization. The implantation window (Days 20–24 of menstrual cycle) is the brief period when the endometrium is receptive. Outside this window, the endometrium actively rejects attachment.

tip.tip: IVF timing is critical—embryo transfer must coincide with the receptive window

cards.text: Describe the three sequential stages of implantation.
cards.answer: Apposition (Day 6)—blastocyst loosely sits on endometrial surface; Adhesion (Day 7)—firm attachment via integrin receptors; Invasion (Days 7–9)—syncytiotrophoblast actively digests through epithelium and stroma.

tip.tip: AAI: Apposition → Adhesion → Invasion (Day 6 → Day 7 → Days 7–9)

cards.text: What is the normal implantation site in the uterus and why?
cards.answer: The posterior wall of the fundus, slightly toward the midline. This site has the richest blood supply and thickest endometrium, optimizing embryonic nourishment.

tip.tip: Posterior fundus = best vascular supply = optimal implantation site

cards.text: How do cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast differ structurally and functionally?
cards.answer: Cytotrophoblast (inner): individual cells, well-defined boundaries, mitotically active. Syncytiotrophoblast (outer): multinucleated mass without cell boundaries, invasive front secreting MMPs. Cyto cells fuse outward to form and feed syncytio.

tip.tip: Cyto = cells (inner, divide); Syncytio = fused mass (outer, invade)

cards.text: What is the critical relationship between cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast?
cards.answer: Cytotrophoblast divides mitotically and feeds cells outward. These cells fuse to form the syncytiotrophoblast, which invades maternal tissue. The syncytiotrophoblast itself does not divide—it grows only by cell fusion from cytotrophoblast.

tip.tip: Remember: Cyto produces → Syncytio invades (no syncytio division)

cards.text: How does the syncytiotrophoblast invade the endometrium?
cards.answer: The syncytiotrophoblast secretes matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) that digest the endometrial extracellular matrix, allowing it to burrow through epithelium, stroma, blood vessels, and glands. It also forms lacunar spaces.

tip.tip: Syncytio = biochemical aggressor: MMPs dissolve its path through tissue

cards.text: What role do endometrial adhesion molecules play in implantation?
cards.answer: The endometrium expresses integrins and selectins and secretes chemokines that guide the blastocyst to the optimal implantation site. These molecules create the receptive environment of the implantation window.

tip.tip: Endometrium doesn't just sit passively—it actively guides and receptive blastocyst attachment
